sup:70620.text:
Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our current offer for your requirements, maintaining our commitment to supporting your business with top-quality service and our extensive product range.

For this offer, we quote a price of €4.96 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net and a contract term of 12 months. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

To provide some background on our pricing calculations, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 10 % of our cost. Furthermore, PPI-C2815 rose 0.8 % in twelve months and is 65 % of our cost.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Florian Gruber
Inside Sales, Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd GmbH

move.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining your position.

Our data shows a different picture on some points:
Our demand forecast for this part has risen 4.2% (fc:360020@2026-09).
Our last 3 orders for this part were at EUR 4.39 per unit (po:4500014467-10, po:4500014389-10, po:4500014329-10).

Please find our proposal below.

We look forward to your reply.

Kind regards
Purchasing
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

move.text:
Dear customer,

We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows. We checked the price history data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. That does not change our position. We have noted your volume forecast and past order history; however, our current pricing reflects our updated cost structure. Our price follows our main cost drivers: PPI-C2815, LCI-C.

We can accept your proposed 36-month contract term. In return, we must ask to keep the payment terms at 30 days, allowing us to offer a revised price of €4.94 per unit. Our current Angebot stands at a price of €4.94 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 36 months. Alternatively, with Zahlungsziel 30 days net: €4.88 per unit. As an alternative option: a price of €4.88 per unit, Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 36 months.

A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the price. Which volume can you commit to? This Angebot remains valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Florian Gruber
Inside Sales, Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd GmbH

decisions.tactician: E0 (pay 90 d, 36 months) and o6 (pay 90 d, 24 months) give our lowest C, both €168,245, well below every 12-month option at about €182,800. E0 also offers the longest commitment, which matches the supplier's main stated need for multi-year volume and planning security. That should help it move off its quote even though the cash value to it is 16 % below its own sheet, which a first anchor can afford. I cite the forecast rise in our demand and our order history at €4.39. I leave out the on-time delivery figure of 85 %: it is defensible, but it is less useful than the volume argument and might sour a supplier that already deprioritises us.

decisions.tactician: o4 has the lowest C among the options (€177,770), level with o3. It keeps the 36-month term the supplier has already accepted and values for planning security, where o3 would drop to 24 months. It moves payment to 60 days, a middle ground the supplier can accept more easily than 90. E0 (45 d) costs us more C at an equivalent value to the supplier. Both standing sheets cost about €19k more than o4. The supplier is still conceding steadily and has not issued a final offer, so countering is better than accepting now. The delivery scorecard (a1) is a new, verified lever that cuts against its cost-driven stance.

decisions.tactician: o2 gives us the lowest C, essentially tied with o1, and is far below the standing offer at €196,970. Its 36-month term speaks directly to the supplier's volume and planning-security needs, which the 'to it' figure does not count, so the real gap to its sheet is smaller than the -6.9 % shown. E0 gives up the 90 d payment for no gain in C. We have eight messages left, so we should keep pushing rather than accept now. No new arguments remain to cite, so the volume commitment does the persuading.
